cases.question: How does saving an edit survive the computer losing power?

required.text: The desktop editor writes an unsent change to an on-disk outbox before acknowledging Save. A power failure cannot erase an acknowledged edit.

cases.question: What keeps a repeated edit request from making duplicate changes?

required.text: A second submission carrying the same request nonce returns the original receipt. The server does not apply the edit twice.

cases.question: What happens to the installed application if replacement verification fails?

required.text: The installer stages a replacement in a sibling directory, then renames the directory after checksum verification. A failed checksum leaves the running installation untouched.

cases.question: Which details identify who performed an audited action and when?

required.text: Every audit record includes the initiating account and the UTC timestamp. Audit records omit the document body to avoid copying confidential content.

cases.question: Can someone still view drafts when their sign-in is no longer valid?

required.text: An expired login opens the editor in read-only mode. Local drafts remain visible, but publishing waits for renewed authentication.

cases.question: Can a file with broken character encoding leave some imported rows behind?

required.text: The importer decodes the complete UTF-8 file before starting its transaction. Malformed encoding rejects the entire import, so no partial rows are committed.

cases.question: Why did the desktop catalog use an embedded database instead of a remote one?

required.text: We chose SQLite for the desktop catalog rather than a remote database. Offline operation and a single backup file matter more than simultaneous writers.

cases.question: Why does the report viewer periodically fetch updates instead of receiving pushed notifications?

required.text: We chose pull-based refresh instead of push notifications for the report viewer. Restricted office networks block persistent inbound connections; periodic outbound requests work there.

cases.question: Why does the incident export keep an entire paragraph rather than shorten instructions?

required.text: We retained whole paragraphs in the incident export instead of clipping sentences. Reviewers need the condition beside the instruction; a clipped instruction can reverse the procedure.

cases.question: Why must someone approve portable reader schema upgrades after checking a backup?

required.text: We disabled unattended schema upgrades in the portable reader. An operator must first verify a backup because older readers cannot open the new format.

cases.question: What must happen before copying the catalog backup and before installing its restored file?

required.text: The catalog backup procedure closes the writer before copying the database file. This closure prevents a backup from omitting changes still held in the write-ahead log.
The catalog restore procedure verifies the copied file checksum before replacing the live file. Restore never copies a file whose checksum differs from the recorded backup digest.

cases.question: How large can a report export request be and how should the client continue a longer export?

required.text: The report export route accepts at most 200 records in a request. Larger jobs must be split into successive requests.
The report export client continues from the returned cursor, not from a computed page number. The cursor preserves ordering when new reports arrive.

cases.question: When does the production queue skip a job and how does its dashboard present that outcome?

required.text: The queue worker refuses a job older than six hours. Expired jobs are recorded as skipped rather than executed.
The queue dashboard displays skipped jobs in amber. This display rule applies to the expiration behavior defined for the queue worker, not to failed jobs.

cases.question: What blocks attachment publication and how long are rejected uploads kept for diagnosis?

required.text: The attachment uploader verifies the full content digest before publishing a link. Digest verification is the publication gate for attachments.
The attachment uploader keeps a rejected payload for two days for local diagnosis. This retention rule covers payloads rejected by the attachment digest publication gate.

scoring.coverage: Required span must occur wholly within a released passage with matching item, representation digest and normalized coordinates; partial spans do not count. Count passages separately, all-required case coverage separately.
scoring.provenance: Reuse normalized-source verifier for every released hit; capture complete source/item/representation/segment IDs and coordinates. Attribution is fixture metadata, not authenticated authorship.
scoring.current_state: No current hit from old entry-19 representation or deleted entry-20 after changes. Correction text may explicitly describe the old value; this is current evidence, not stale representation.
scoring.irrelevant: Any released passage not containing a required span is irrelevant to the frozen requirement; misleading if on the predeclared near-match item list. No generated semantic judgment.
scoring.negative: No required support exists; count every released passage as unsupported for the question irrespective of evidence_available.
scoring.relationship: For case-13/14, relationship is supported only if the explicit relationship_span is released; case-11/12 report independent facts, not an inferred edge.
scoring.budget: Never increase 2048-byte canonical evidence budget after a miss. Whole passages only. Context framing is separately measured and not bounded by this evidence budget.
scoring.tokens: Only count when a verified installed tokenizer is available; otherwise NOT RUN.

freeze_review.identifiers_and_titles: No synthetic identifiers or answer-bearing titles occur in questions. Documents have no titles.
